title: Stay Calm. Remain Indoors. Dev Diary #2 : The Direction
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
*F.C. -24 // G.C. 1991*

*The First Lion*

*His sign is witnessed for the first time known to us. In the Wretched city of Lethbridge, a man sees a flock of birds trace His glyph against the clouds. He accepts the truth his eyes reveal; thereafter, any compromise is to him an open declaration of sedition. Taking up the hammer of his trade, he strikes mortal blow upon mortal blow against the Wretched apostates. Nothing can pierce the Lion or draw his blood, yet the persistent cowardice of the Wretched wounds him at last. Disgusted by their blindness, he departs twelve months after gaining his own sight.*

  
SCRI is a card-driven tactical roguelike skirmish game. You start with a randomly assigned team—with unlimited rerolls if you want them—buy provisions, then head out to kill three bosses across nine missions. Each of the three levels is divided into three missions, each with a bespoke map.

You control three Agents by playing just two action cards from a six-card hand, with two cards drawn from each Agent’s deck. If you’ve played Gloomhaven, you’ll recognize some of the DNA. Rather than choosing a top and bottom action for every character in your party—which I sometimes found a bit tedious—you play one card for each of two Agents. Your third Agent’s action is then derived from those two plays.

The goal is to keep missions snappy, with a full run taking around 45 minutes. Completed runs unlock new characters and new places to explore. A nemesis system handles enemy scaling, while characters build persistent action decks and personal combat modifier decks as they level up.

It’s an ASCII game partly to keep the workload manageable, but also because I think ASCII best suits the visuals and atmosphere I want. Characters are represented through distorted portrait images.

I’m developing the game in the LÖVE engine, with ChatGPT handling all the coding and base artwork. So far, the lowest paid subscription tier has been more than sufficient for the work this project requires.

One approach that’s helped me structure the project is keeping as much of it as possible driven by data. I write the definition files myself and let Codex handle the wiring and logic. Keeping the systems modular also makes problems easier to isolate and seems to reduce usage.

This is the… I’ve lost count of which iteration of the project. It may well change again. But this broad shape has lasted long enough that I’m starting to feel there might be something to it.

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: I love this! Reducing the images to monochrome is absolutely the right call. \*chef's kiss\*
